skills.name: autoresearch-optimizer
skills.description: Autonomous experiment loop that turns Hubsy into a self-improving researcher. Form a hypothesis, modify a target asset or prompt, run a fixed evaluation metric, and keep the change only if the score improves or revert if it is worse. Modeled on karpathy/autoresearch (edits train.py against a fixed val_bpb evaluator while a program.md direction file steers the loop), generalized to prompts, configs, and code. Use for overnight/autonomous optimization, iterative experimentation, prompt tuning, and benchmark-driven change review.

skills.name: google-workspace-cli
skills.description: Drive Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets, Docs, Chat, and other Google Workspace APIs from the terminal using the gws CLI (googleworkspace/cli). Every gws command returns structured JSON and the command surface is built dynamically from Google's Discovery Service. Use whenever the user wants to check or send email, manage calendar events and agendas, list or upload Drive files, read or write spreadsheet cells and rows, edit documents, or send Google Chat messages.

skills.name: anthropic-skills-engine
skills.description: Author, structure, and consume skills per the official Agent Skills Specification (agentskills.io) as implemented by anthropics/skills: a folder with a SKILL.md combining YAML frontmatter (name, description, optional license/compatibility/metadata) with a Markdown instruction body, organized for progressive disclosure across scripts/, references/, and assets/. Leverages Anthropic's enterprise skills for document processing (pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx) and brand-guidelines styling. Use when building or validating a custom skill, processing/generating documents, or applying on-brand colors and typography.
triggers: how do I format a skill

skills.name: context-mode
skills.description: Context window optimization for Hubsy via the context-mode MCP server (mksglu/context-mode). Enforces mandatory routing rules to keep raw tool output out of context: intercept heavy web fetches (ctx_fetch_and_index), sandbox large file reads (ctx_execute/ctx_execute_file/ctx_batch_execute), and use intent-driven search (ctx_index, ctx_search) so only distilled results reach the context window (~98% reduction). Also tracks edits, git ops, tasks, and decisions in SQLite/FTS5 for session continuity across compaction. Use for long-running sessions, token/context pressure, reading big files or pages, or when a search would replace a full read.

skills.name: design-taste-frontend
skills.description: Anti-slop frontend design engine derived from taste-skill (github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill). Gives the agent good design taste so generated UI does not look generic or templated. Defines three adjustable dials (DESIGN_VARIANCE 1-10 perfect-symmetry-to-artsy-chaos, MOTION_INTENSITY 1-10 static-to-cinematic, VISUAL_DENSITY 1-10 art-gallery-to-cockpit), typography scale discipline (display text-4xl/6xl tracking-tighter, body max-w-[65ch], serif/Fraunces/Instrument_Serif restrictions), spacing rhythm (py-16/24 daily app, py-32/48 art gallery), interaction polish (state cycles, motivated motion, reduced-motion, spring physics), color calibration (one accent, no AI-purple, premium-consumer beige-ban), layout diversification (anti-center bias, zigzag cap, bento rhythm, eyebrow max 1-per-3-sections), and a strict pre-flight anti-tell checklist. Use when building or redesigning landing pages, portfolios, heroes, bento grids, pricing pages, or any frontend that should not look like LLM-default output.
triggers: not all landing pages look the same

skills.name: humanizer
skills.description: Rewrite AI-sounding text so it reads like the writer without changing what it says. Scans prose for AI writing patterns (overused vocabulary, rigid syntax, rule-of-three triads, dramatic one-line closers, not-X-but-Y contrasts, dashes everywhere, inflated significance, sales language, stock AI words, bold labels, chatbot residue, knowledge-limit disclaimers) and rewrites it into a natural human voice. Based on blader/humanizer (github.com/blader/humanizer, MIT, v3.1.0) and Wikipedia's Sign of AI writing. Supports pasted-text mode, file mode (prose-only edits, code preserved), and embedded mode (commit messages, PRs, documents). Use when humanizing, de-AI-ing, or editing any text that sounds machine-generated, whether for an assignment, essay, blog post, email, comment, or response.
